name: Google Docs, Sheets & Slides
summary: Google's browser-based editors. Documents live in Google's own format inside Drive; the .gdoc files in a synced folder are only links to them.

factors: Documents exist only as records in Google's cloud until you export them
Sharing links and comment threads scattered through years of email
Apps Script automations, and Forms that feed Sheets
Effortless real-time collaboration that everyone already knows how to use

export.summary: Google Takeout converts everything to Office or OpenDocument formats in one go. Conversion is good for ordinary documents and loses the Google-only parts.

methods.name: Google Takeout
methods.detail: Select Drive, choose the export formats (.docx, .xlsx and .pptx, or OpenDocument), and download the archives. Folder structure is preserved.

methods.name: Data export for Workspace administrators
methods.detail: An administrator can export every user's data for the whole organisation in one operation.

methods.name: rclone
methods.detail: Copies a Drive to any destination and converts Google documents to the format you choose on the way. Scriptable and resumable, which matters for large Drives.

caveats: Files shared with you but owned by someone else are not included; make copies of the ones you need
Apps Script, Forms logic and connected sheets do not survive
Sharing permissions are not carried over

paths.verdict: With Nextcloud, this is the closest open equivalent of documents that live in the browser and are shared by link.

import.summary: Export from Google as OpenDocument or Office formats, upload the folders to your file platform and open them in the browser. Check spreadsheets that use Google-specific functions such as QUERY, IMPORTRANGE or GOOGLEFINANCE.

lost: Existing share links, which all have to be recreated

paths.verdict: Choose it if most of what you exchange with the outside world is Office files.

import.summary: Export from Google in Office formats, which ONLYOFFICE uses natively, and upload them to your file platform. Check spreadsheets that use Google-specific functions.

paths.verdict: Fine if you mostly write alone and can give up editing together in a browser.

import.summary: Export from Google as OpenDocument and open the files locally. The files then live wherever you keep them: a synced folder, a server, a USB stick.

lost: Google-only spreadsheet functions, Apps Script and Forms

paths.verdict: Fine for writing alone in Office formats; you give up editing together in a browser.

import.summary: Export from Google in Office formats, which it edits natively, and open the files locally. Check spreadsheets that use Google-specific functions.

lost: Google-only spreadsheet functions, Apps Script and Forms
